# DockerCli* Adapter Authoring Reference

All files rooted at `/Users/mariotoffia/progs/github/FluentDocker/`. Namespaces: components live in `FluentDocker.Drivers.Docker.Cli.Components`; base in `FluentDocker.Drivers.Docker.Cli`; binary in `FluentDocker.Drivers.Docker.Cli.Binary`.

---
## 1. DockerCliDriverBase — constructor signature & fields
File: `FluentDocker/Drivers/Docker/Cli/DockerCliDriverBase.cs`

Class: `public abstract class DockerCliDriverBase` (line 21).

Protected members / fields available to adapters:
- `protected const string DockerCommand = "docker";` (line 26) — the logical command name passed to the resolver. NOTE: this constant is always `"docker"` even when the user configures a custom `BinaryName` (finch/nerdctl); the resolver maps it to the real client binary via `MainDockerClient`.
- `protected DriverContext Context { get; private set; }` (line 31) — set by `Initialize`.
- `protected ILogger Logger { get; private set; } = NullLogger.Instance;` (line 37) — category = concrete type FQN; defaults to NullLogger until `Initialize`.
- `protected IBinaryResolver BinaryResolver { get; private set; }` (line 42).

Constructors (line 47, 55):
```csharp
protected DockerCliDriverBase()                              // no resolver (BinaryResolver stays null -> falls back to literal "docker")
protected DockerCliDriverBase(IBinaryResolver binaryResolver) => BinaryResolver = binaryResolver;
```
EVERY existing component uses the resolver ctor pattern, e.g. `DockerCliVolumeDriver.cs:24`:
```csharp
public DockerCliVolumeDriver(IBinaryResolver binaryResolver) : base(binaryResolver) { }
```
So a NEW adapter MUST declare `public DockerCliXxxDriver(IBinaryResolver binaryResolver) : base(binaryResolver) { }`.

Initialize (virtual; overridable but normally not overridden by components):
- `public virtual void Initialize(DriverContext context)` (line 61) — null-checks context, sets `Context`, creates `Logger = context.LoggerFactory.CreateLogger(GetType())`.
- `public virtual void Initialize(DriverContext context, IBinaryResolver binaryResolver)` (line 73) — also sets `BinaryResolver`.

The driver pack (`DockerCliDriverPack.cs:72-93`) constructs each component with `new DockerCliXxxDriver(_binaryResolver)` then calls `.Initialize(context)` (the single-arg overload — resolver already supplied via ctor). A new adapter follows the exact same two-step lifecycle. Register it by interface in `_drivers[typeof(IXxxDriver)] = _xxxDriver;` (pack line ~96+).

---
## 2. ExecuteCommandAsync — EXACT signatures & behavior
File: `DockerCliDriverBase.cs`. Return type is ALWAYS `Task<SimpleCommandResult>`.

Three overloads (all `protected async Task<SimpleCommandResult>`):
```csharp
// line 139
ExecuteCommandAsync(string arguments, CancellationToken cancellationToken)
// line 150 — pipes stdinData to the process stdin
ExecuteCommandAsync(string arguments, string stdinData, CancellationToken cancellationToken)
// line 162 — adds extra env vars
ExecuteCommandAsync(string arguments, IDictionary<string,string> environment, CancellationToken cancellationToken)
```
Internal flow (line 141-144): resolves `(binaryPath, sudo, sudoPassword)` via `ResolveBinaryInfo()`, prepends global args via `BuildGlobalArgs(Context)`, then `ExecuteProcessAsync(...)`.

`SimpleCommandResult` (line 474-495) — the return DTO, mutable get/set:
```csharp
public class SimpleCommandResult {
  public bool   Success  { get; set; }  // == (ExitCode == 0)
  public string Output   { get; set; }  // full stdout (UTF-8, ReadToEndAsync)
  public string Error    { get; set; }  // full stderr (UTF-8)
  public int    ExitCode { get; set; }
}
```
ExecuteProcessAsync behavior (line 179-270), important guarantees:
- `Success = (process.ExitCode == 0)` (line 245). On caught exception returns `{Success=false, Error=ex.Message, ExitCode=-1}` (line 259-264) — it does NOT throw for normal failures; only `OperationCanceledException` is rethrown (after killing the child, line 251-256).
- stdout + stderr read CONCURRENTLY (line 234-238) to avoid pipe-buffer deadlock; encoding forced UTF-8 (line 207-208).
- `UseShellExecute=false`, `CreateNoWindow=true`. Arguments are passed as a single `Arguments` string — there is NO array-arg API, hence quoting is the caller's responsibility (see §3).

Adapter pattern: always `var result = await ExecuteCommandAsync(args, cancellationToken).ConfigureAwait(false);` then branch on `result.Success`.

---
## 3. QuoteArgumentIfNeeded — signature & escaping (SECURITY-CRITICAL)
File: `DockerCliDriverBase.cs:455`.
```csharp
protected static string QuoteArgumentIfNeeded(string argument)
```
Behavior (line 455-466):
- `null` or empty -> returns the literal two-char string `"\"\""` (i.e. `""`), NOT null.
- Quoting triggered when the arg contains ANY shell metacharacter from the SearchValues set (line 448-449): space, tab, `;`, `&`, `|`, `>`, `<`, `"`, `'`, `$`, backtick, `!`, `*`, `?`. Membership test: `argument.AsSpan().IndexOfAny(ShellMetaCharacters) >= 0`.
- If no metachar -> returns the argument UNCHANGED (unquoted). So plain tokens like `nginx:latest` pass through verbatim.
- When quoting: escapes backslashes first then double-quotes: `argument.Replace("\\", "\\\\").Replace("\"", "\\\"")`, then wraps in `"..."`. Resulting form: `"{escaped}"`.

Security-test implications: an input containing `;`, `&&`, `$(...)`, backticks, `|`, `>` etc. WILL be quoted and the metachars neutralized (the whole thing becomes a single quoted token, no shell because `UseShellExecute=false`). Inputs WITHOUT metachars are NOT quoted — fine since no shell is involved, but injection of a leading `-` (flag injection) is NOT handled by this method; use `--` separators where the CLI supports them if you need that. Note: `=` and `-`, `/`, `:`, `.`, `@` are NOT in the metachar set, so `key=value`, paths, image refs pass unquoted unless they also contain a metachar.

It is `static` and `protected` — directly callable from any derived adapter. New adapters MUST route every user-supplied value (names, filters, labels, ids, paths used as args) through it, matching existing usage e.g. `DockerCliVolumeDriver.cs:39,44,50,53,87,121,126,174` and `DockerCliImageDriver.cs:41,69,102,...`.

Other quoting idioms seen: format strings quoted inline as literals `--format "{{json .}}"` (volume ls line 116, image list line 208, stream line 75/112). Output file paths sometimes quoted manually with `\"{outputPath}\"` instead of QuoteArgumentIfNeeded (image Save line 139, Load line 166, Import line 217-218) — prefer QuoteArgumentIfNeeded for new code for consistency/safety.

---
## 4. Building a command string & mapping to CommandResponse + CreateErrorContext
Two build idioms:
- List<string> + join (volume Create `DockerCliVolumeDriver.cs:36-55`, image Build `DockerCliImageDriver.cs:99-136`): `var args = new List<string>{ "volume","create" }; ... args.Add($"--driver {QuoteArgumentIfNeeded(...)}"); ... ExecuteCommandAsync(string.Join(" ", args), ct)`.
- String concat (volume Remove `:84-87`, image Remove `Operations.cs:55-60`, stream BuildStreamLogsArgs `:37-50`): `var args = "volume rm"; if(force) args += " --force"; args += $" {QuoteArgumentIfNeeded(name)}";`.

CommandResponse mapping (`Model/Drivers/CommandResponse.cs`). `CommandResponse<T>` has init-only props: `Success, Data, Error, ErrorCode, ErrorContext, ExitCode, Output`. Factory methods:
```csharp
CommandResponse<T>.Ok(T data)                                   // line 51, ExitCode=0
CommandResponse<T>.Ok(T data, string output)                    // line 64
CommandResponse<T>.Fail(string error, string errorCode=null, int exitCode=-1)        // line 78
CommandResponse<T>.Fail(string error, string errorCode, ErrorContext context, int exitCode=-1)  // line 92
```
Canonical adapter method skeleton (copy verbatim — from volume/image drivers):
```csharp
public async Task<CommandResponse<TResult>> XxxAsync(
    DriverContext context, /* params */, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)
{
  try
  {
    var args = /* build */;
    var result = await ExecuteCommandAsync(args, cancellationToken).ConfigureAwait(false);
    if (!result.Success)
    {
      return CommandResponse<TResult>.Fail(
          result.Error ?? "Xxx failed",
          ErrorCodes.Area.XxxFailed,
          CreateErrorContext(context, "OperationName", result),
          result.ExitCode);
    }
    return CommandResponse<TResult>.Ok(/* parsed Data */);
  }
  catch (Exception ex)
  {
    return CommandResponse<TResult>.Fail(ex.Message, ErrorCodes.Area.XxxFailed);
  }
}
```
Notes on conventions:
- The OUTER try/catch returns a 2-arg `Fail(ex.Message, errorCode)` (no ErrorContext) — exit code defaults to -1.
- The `!result.Success` branch uses `result.Error ?? "<fallback>"` and the 4-arg `Fail(...)` WITH `CreateErrorContext` and `result.ExitCode`. Some methods (image Tag `Operations.cs:32`, Remove `:66`, Pull-fail `DockerCliImageDriver.cs:45`) omit the ErrorContext (use 2-arg Fail) — both are accepted in the codebase, but prefer the 4-arg with context for new management/runtime ops.
- For `Unit` results (no payload) return `CommandResponse<Unit>.Ok(Unit.Default)` (volume Remove `:100`). `Unit` is from `FluentDocker.Common`.

CreateErrorContext helpers (`DockerCliDriverBase.cs`):
```csharp
// line 382 (static)
protected static ErrorContext CreateErrorContext(DriverContext context, string operation, SimpleCommandResult result)
// line 400 (instance, uses this.Context)
protected ErrorContext CreateErrorContext(string operation, SimpleCommandResult result)
```
The static one maps: `new ErrorContext(operation){ DriverId=context.DriverId, Host=context.Host, ExitCode=result.ExitCode, StdOut=result.Output, StdErr=result.Error }` (line 384-391). Existing adapters call the STATIC overload passing the method's `context` param: `CreateErrorContext(context, "CreateVolume", result)` — DO THIS (the param `context` is the per-call DriverContext, distinct from the field `Context`). `ErrorContext` (`Model/Drivers/ErrorContext.cs`) also has `OperationId`, `Operation`, `Metadata`, `Timestamp` (auto UtcNow) but CreateErrorContext does not populate OperationId.

ErrorCodes: referenced as `ErrorCodes.Volume.CreateFailed`, `ErrorCodes.Image.PullFailed`, `ErrorCodes.General.Unknown`, `ErrorCodes.Container.AttachFailed`, etc. (from `FluentDocker.Common`). Pick/add the matching area+name.

---
## 5. Streaming-stdout mechanism — ALREADY EXISTS (do NOT add)
File: `DockerCliDriverBase.cs:278`. There IS a built-in streaming primitive:
```csharp
protected async IAsyncEnumerable<string> ExecuteStreamingCommandAsync(
    string arguments, [EnumeratorCancellation] CancellationToken cancellationToken)
```
Behavior (line 278-328): resolves binary + global args + sudo (sudo via stdin password only, NoPassword/Password handled), starts process with redirected stdout, loops `reader.ReadLineAsync(cancellationToken)` yielding each line until null or cancellation; `finally` calls `KillProcessSafely(process, Logger)` (line 326) to avoid orphans. It does NOT capture/return stderr or exit code — line-oriented stdout only. Sudo with Password writes the password line then closes stdin (line 305-309); it does NOT support piping additional stdin data while streaming.

How adapters consume it (`DockerCliStreamDriver.cs`):
```csharp
public async IAsyncEnumerable<string> StreamLogsAsync(DriverContext context, string containerId,
    StreamLogsConfig config=null, [EnumeratorCancellation] CancellationToken ct=default)
{
  var args = BuildStreamLogsArgs(containerId, config);
  await foreach (var line in ExecuteStreamingCommandAsync(args, ct))
    yield return line;            // line 63-66
}
```
For JSON-per-line streams, deserialize inside the loop and swallow parse errors with `Logger.LogDebug` (events `:86-101`, stats `:131-145`). ANSI-prefix handling for `docker stats` streaming is done in `ParseStreamStatsLine` (`:156-212`) by slicing `json.IndexOf('{')`..`LastIndexOf('}')` — reuse this approach if your stream emits cursor escape codes.

IMPORTANT: the IMAGE PULL path does NOT stream. `DockerCliImageDriver.PullAsync` (`DockerCliImageDriver.cs:31-58`) runs a normal blocking `ExecuteCommandAsync("pull ...")` and IGNORES the `IProgress<ImagePullProgress> progress` parameter entirely — no per-line progress is parsed. So there is currently NO streaming-progress mechanism for pull/push/build; if your NEW adapter needs incremental progress callbacks you must build it yourself on top of `ExecuteStreamingCommandAsync` (parse each line into a progress event and call `progress?.Report(...)`). The base class already gives you the line stream; you only add the parsing/Report layer.

Two other process primitives exist for long-running attach (not line streaming):
- `protected AttachResult ExecuteAttachProcess(string arguments)` (line 333) — returns raw `InputStream/OutputStream/ErrorStream` + `AttachedProcess`; sudo-with-password NOT supported (passes null, line 341). Used by `DockerCliStreamDriver.AttachAsync` (`:233`) which wraps it synchronously in `Task.FromResult(CommandResponse<AttachResult>.Ok(result))`.

---
## 6. How sudo / binary path are threaded
Private resolver (`DockerCliDriverBase.cs:124-131`):
```csharp
private (string BinaryPath, SudoMechanism Sudo, string SudoPassword) ResolveBinaryInfo()
{
  if (BinaryResolver == null) return (DockerCommand, SudoMechanism.None, null); // literal "docker"
  var binary = BinaryResolver.Resolve(DockerCommand);
  return (binary.FqPath, binary.Sudo, binary.SudoPassword);
}
```
So binary path comes from `DockerBinary.FqPath` (= `Path.Combine(Path, Binary)`, `DockerBinary.cs:73`) and sudo config comes from the same `DockerBinary`. Adapters NEVER touch this directly — they just call `ExecuteCommandAsync`/`ExecuteStreamingCommandAsync` and it is threaded automatically.

Sudo execution (`DockerCliDriverBase.cs:414-423`) — password NEVER on command line:
```csharp
private static (string FileName, string Arguments, string PasswordForStdin) BuildSudoCommand(
    string binaryPath, string arguments, SudoMechanism sudo, string sudoPassword)
=> sudo switch {
    SudoMechanism.NoPassword => ("sudo", $"{binaryPath} {arguments}", null),
    SudoMechanism.Password   => ("sudo", $"-S {binaryPath} {arguments}", sudoPassword),
    _                        => (binaryPath, arguments, null) };
```
Password is written to stdin (`process.StandardInput.WriteLineAsync(passwordForStdin)`, line 224/307). `SudoMechanism` enum (from `FluentDocker.Model.Common`) values: `None`, `NoPassword`, `Password`.

Binary resolution chain (`Binary/`):
- `IBinaryResolver` (`IBinaryResolver.cs`): props `DockerBinary[] Binaries`, `MainDockerClient`, `MainDockerCompose`, `MainDockerCli`, `bool IsDockerComposeAvailable`; methods `DockerBinary Resolve(string binary)` and `string ResolveBinaryPath(string dockerCommand)`.
- `DockerBinariesResolver` (`DockerBinariesResolver.cs`) ctors: `(BinaryConfiguration, ILoggerFactory=null)` (line 35) and `(SudoMechanism, string password, params string[] paths)` (line 68). `Resolve("docker")` maps `DockerBinaryType.DockerClient -> MainDockerClient` (line 94-107); throws `FluentDockerException` if not found. `ResolveBinaryPath` prepends `sudo`/`sudo -S` EXCEPT on Windows or `SudoMechanism.None` (line 115-125) — but note the BASE class does NOT use `ResolveBinaryPath`; it uses `Resolve(...).FqPath` + its own `BuildSudoCommand`, so sudo prefixing happens in the base, not the resolver, for command execution.
- The pack builds the resolver from `DriverContext` (`DockerCliDriverPack.cs:61-69`): `BinaryConfiguration { Sudo=context.Sudo, SudoPassword=context.SudoPassword, DefaultShell=context.DefaultShell, BinaryName = context.BinaryName ?? "docker", SearchPaths=context.SearchPaths }`. Custom engine support (finch/nerdctl) flows through `BinaryName`; the resolved binary is still typed `DockerClient` so `Resolve("docker")` returns it (`DockerBinariesResolver.cs:143-146`, 178-181).
- `DockerBinary.Translate` (`DockerBinary.cs:57-68`) only knows `docker`/`docker.exe`, `dockercli`/`.exe`, `compose`; throws `ArgumentException` otherwise. Docker Machine/Toolbox/standalone docker-compose removed in v3.

Global flags threading: `BuildGlobalArgs(DriverContext)` (`DockerCliDriverBase.cs:90-114`, public static) emits `-H {Host}` and TLS flags (`--tlsverify`/`--tls`, `--tlscacert/--tlscert/--tlskey` from `CertificatePath`+ca.pem/cert.pem/key.pem) and is auto-prepended to args inside every Execute* method (line 142-143, 281-282, 336-337). Returns "" when Context null or Host empty. Adapters do not call this.

---
## 7. DriverContext usage in adapter methods
`DriverContext` (`Model/Drivers/DriverContext.cs`) is passed as the FIRST parameter to EVERY public adapter method (matching the driver interfaces). There are TWO DriverContext references in play:
- The METHOD PARAMETER `context` — pass this to `CreateErrorContext(context, "Op", result)`. This is the per-operation context (carries `DriverId`, `Host`, `OperationId`, `Metadata`).
- The FIELD `Context` (capital C, `DockerCliDriverBase.cs:31`) — set during `Initialize`, used internally by Execute* for `BuildGlobalArgs(Context)`. Adapters normally do NOT read the field directly; they receive `context` as a param. In existing components the param and the field are the same instance (pack passes one context), but the convention is: USE THE PARAMETER for error context.

Key `DriverContext` fields adapters may read off the param: `DriverId`, `Host`, `CertificatePath`, `VerifyTls`, `OperationId`, `Metadata`, `Sudo`/`SudoPassword`/`DefaultShell` (already consumed by resolver), `BinaryName`, `SearchPaths`, `ConnectionTimeout`/`RequestTimeout`/`ApiVersion` (API-driver only — irrelevant to CLI adapters), `LoggerFactory`. `LoggerFactory` defaults to `NullLoggerFactory.Instance`.

Interface method signature convention (e.g. `IVolumeDriver` in `FluentDocker/Drivers/IVolumeDriver.cs:13`): all return `Task<CommandResponse<T>>`, first param `DriverContext context`, last param `CancellationToken cancellationToken = default`. Streaming methods return `IAsyncEnumerable<T>` with `[EnumeratorCancellation] CancellationToken cancellationToken = default` (see `IStreamDriver`).

---
## 8. CliPruneOutputParser — for prune-result mapping
File: `FluentDocker/Drivers/CliPruneOutputParser.cs`, namespace `FluentDocker.Drivers`, `public static partial class CliPruneOutputParser`. Static entry points (use these to map `result.Output` -> typed prune result, see usage volume `DockerCliVolumeDriver.cs:210-211`, image `Operations.cs:117-118`):
```csharp
ImagePruneResult   ParseImagePruneOutput(string output)    // line 23
NetworkPruneResult ParseNetworkPruneOutput(string output)  // line 82
VolumePruneResult  ParseVolumePruneOutput(string output)   // line 140
SystemPruneResult  ParseSystemPruneOutput(string output)   // line 201
```
All are exception-safe: catch -> `LogDebug` (NullLogger) -> return a fresh empty result (e.g. line 71-74). They parse human-readable docker/podman prune text: section headers `Deleted Images:/Networks:/Volumes:/Containers:/build cache`, `deleted:`/`untagged:` lines, bare image-id regex `^(?:sha256:)?[a-f0-9]{12,}$` (line 390), simple-name regex `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*$` (line 17-18), and `Total reclaimed space:` -> bytes via `DockerCliSystemDriver.ParseHumanReadableBytes(value)` (line 352). Lines starting WARNING / "This will remove" / "Are you sure" are ignored (line 324-329). For a NEW prune-style adapter, prefer `--force`/`-f` in args (existing: `volume prune --force` line 201, `image prune -f` `Operations.cs:99`) to avoid the interactive confirmation prompt, then feed `result.Output` to the matching parser.

## 9. Adapter file template / checklist (management + runtime)
1. `public class DockerCliXxxDriver : DockerCliDriverBase, IXxxDriver` (or `partial class` split across `DockerCliXxxDriver.cs` + `DockerCliXxxDriver.Operations.cs` if >500 lines — see image driver split; both parts share the same partial and the `LineSeparators` const is declared once, in Operations: `private static readonly char[] LineSeparators = ['\n','\r'];` `Operations.cs:15`).
2. Ctor: `public DockerCliXxxDriver(IBinaryResolver binaryResolver) : base(binaryResolver) { }`.
3. Each op: `try { build args (QuoteArgumentIfNeeded every dynamic value); ExecuteCommandAsync(args, ct).ConfigureAwait(false); if(!result.Success) return Fail(result.Error ?? "...", ErrorCodes...., CreateErrorContext(context, "Op", result), result.ExitCode); parse result.Output; return Ok(data); } catch(Exception ex){ return Fail(ex.Message, ErrorCodes....); }`.
4. JSON list output: request `--format "{{json .}}"`, split on `result.Output.Split(LineSeparators, StringSplitOptions.RemoveEmptyEntries)`, per line `JsonSerializer.Deserialize<T>(line, JsonHelper.CaseInsensitiveOptions)` inside try/catch logging `Logger.LogError`/`LogDebug` (volume ls `DockerCliVolumeDriver.cs:141-156`). `JsonHelper` is `FluentDocker.Common.JsonHelper` with `CaseInsensitiveOptions`, `ParseElement`, and `JsonElement` extensions `GetStringOrDefault` (stream driver uses these).
5. Streaming op: `await foreach (var line in ExecuteStreamingCommandAsync(args, ct)) { ... yield return ...; }`; mark method `[EnumeratorCancellation] CancellationToken cancellationToken = default`.
6. Wire into `DockerCliDriverPack.InitializeAsync` (`DockerCliDriverPack.cs`): add field, `new DockerCliXxxDriver(_binaryResolver)`, `.Initialize(context)`, and `_drivers[typeof(IXxxDriver)] = _xxxDriver;`.

Usings commonly needed: `System`, `System.Collections.Generic`, `System.Linq`, `System.Text`, `System.Text.Json`, `System.Threading`, `System.Threading.Tasks`, `System.Runtime.CompilerServices` (for `[EnumeratorCancellation]`), `FluentDocker.Common`, `FluentDocker.Drivers.Docker.Cli.Binary`, `FluentDocker.Model.Drivers`, the relevant `FluentDocker.Model.*` for the result types, `Microsoft.Extensions.Logging`.

## Executive summary (READ FIRST — affects the whole Phase 7b design)

**There is NO YAML serializer in this repo, and the v3.1 "compose builder" does NOT emit YAML at all.** Two separate, *disconnected* worlds exist:

1. **A POCO compose model** (`FluentDocker/Model/Compose/*.cs`) + a fluent **`ComposeServiceBuilder`** (`FluentDocker/Builders/ComposeServiceBuilder.cs`) that *populate a `ComposeServiceDefinition` object graph in memory*. **These are orphaned scaffolding** — `ComposeServiceBuilder` has an `internal` ctor (`ComposeServiceBuilder.cs:21`) and is referenced **nowhere** outside its own file (verified by repo-wide grep). There is no code that turns a `ComposeServiceDefinition` into YAML text. No `ToYaml`, no `ISerializer`, no template engine, no `services:`-emitting code exists anywhere in `FluentDocker/`.

2. **The actual v3.1 compose pipeline** (`IComposeBuilder` → `ComposeBuilder` → `IComposeDriver`/`DockerCliComposeDriver`) is **purely file-path + CLI-flag based**. It never reads or writes YAML *content*; it only passes `-f <file>` / `-p <project>` to the `docker compose` CLI. Parsing is limited to CLI *output* (JSON from `ps`/`images`, text tables from `top`) — never the compose file body.

Confirmed: `FluentDocker/FluentDocker.csproj:29-32` packages are only `Microsoft.Extensions.Logging.Abstractions`, `Microsoft.SourceLink.GitHub`, `SharpCompress`, `System.IO.Pipelines`. **No YamlDotNet.** Repo-wide grep for `YamlDotNet|ISerializer|ToYaml|YamlMember|Razor|Scriban|template` in `FluentDocker/` returns nothing relevant.

**Implication for Phase 7b:** "emitting a `models:` element via the EXISTING compose builder" requires deciding which builder is "the compose builder." The *only* builder wired into `Builder.UseCompose(...)` is the file-path-based `IComposeBuilder`, which has no model and no emitter. To emit `models:` you must EITHER (a) build a YAML emitter for the orphaned `ComposeServiceDefinition` model and wire `ComposeServiceBuilder` in, OR (b) add `models:` modeling to `ComposeServiceDefinition` + `ComposeServiceBuilder` and a new emitter. There is no existing emit path to "slot into." See §2.

---

## (1) How the compose builder models services & emits/loads YAML

### 1a. The POCO model (in-memory only, no (de)serialization)
- `FluentDocker/Model/Compose/ComposeServiceDefinition.cs:27` — `public sealed class ComposeServiceDefinition`. Plain POCO, one property per compose service key: `Name` (string, line 29), `Image` (line 275), `Restart` (RestartPolicy, line 31), `Environment` (`IDictionary<string,string>`, line 220), `DependsOn` (`IList<string>`, line 145), `Ports` (`IList<IPortsDefinition>`, line 349), `Volumes` (`IList<IServiceVolumeDefinition>`, line 416, get-only), `Networks` (`IList<ServiceNetworkDefinition>`, line 336), `Secrets`, `ConfigLong`, `HealthCheck`, etc. **No serialization attributes** (no `JsonPropertyName`, no `YamlMember`) anywhere in `Model/Compose/`.
- The model uses a **short/long marker-interface pattern** for polymorphic list entries:
  - `FluentDocker/Model/Compose/IPortsDefinition.cs` — empty marker interface `public interface IPortsDefinition {}`.
  - `PortsShortDefinition : IPortsDefinition` (single `public string Entry { get; set; }`) and `PortsLongDefinition : IPortsDefinition` (structured `Target/Published/Mode/Protocol`).
  - `IServiceVolumeDefinition.cs` — empty marker; `ShortServiceVolumeDefinition` (`Entry`) and `LongServiceVolumeDefinition` (`Source`/`Target`/`IsReadOnly`/`Options`).
  - **This is the exact pattern a new `models:` binding should follow** (see §2/§4).

### 1b. The fluent service builder (populates the POCO; orphaned)
- `FluentDocker/Builders/ComposeServiceBuilder.cs:17` — `public class ComposeServiceBuilder`. Holds `private readonly ComposeServiceDefinition _config = new();` (line 19). ctor `internal ComposeServiceBuilder(string name) => _config.Name = name;` (line 21).
- Fluent methods all return `ComposeServiceBuilder` (self) and mutate `_config`: `Image(string)` (23), `Volume(...)` (37, 58), `Restart(RestartPolicy)` (66), `Environment(params string[])` (77, parses `name=value` or even/odd pairs), `DependsOn(params string[])` (108), `Ports(int target, int published, PortMode mode, string protocol)` (117) and `Ports(params string[])` (125).
- **No `Build()`/`ToYaml()`/emit method.** There is no way to extract YAML or even to hand the `_config` to anyone. This builder is currently dead code — the natural home for a fluent `.Models(...)` per-service binding once wired, but it isn't wired today.

### 1c. The ACTUAL compose builder (file-path based; the one users call)
- Entry point: `Builder.UseCompose(Action<IComposeBuilder> configure)` at `FluentDocker/Builders/Builder.cs:146-158`. It does `var builder = new ComposeBuilder(_currentKernel, _currentDriverId); configure(builder);` and queues `builder.ExecuteAsync`.
- Also surfaced via `DockerCliFluentBuilder.UseCompose(Action<IComposeBuilder> configure)` at `DockerCliFluentBuilder.cs:63` (delegates to `_inner.UseCompose`).
- Interface: `FluentDocker/Builders/BuilderInterfaces.cs:97` — `public interface IComposeBuilder`. ALL methods are file/flag oriented and return `IComposeBuilder`:
  - `WithComposeFile(string path)` (102), `WithComposeFiles(params string[] paths)` (107), `WithProjectName(string name)` (112), `WithEnvironment(...)` (118/123), `WithEnvFile(string path)` (128), `WithBuild` (133), `WithForceRecreate` (138), `WithRemoveOrphans` (143), `ForServices(params string[])` (148), `WithRemoveVolumes` (153), `WithRemoveImages` (158), `WithTimeout` (163), `WithScale(string,int)` (169), `WithNoDeps` (174), `WithNoStart` (179), `WithPull` (184), `WithWait` (189), `WithWaitTimeout` (194), `WithProfiles(params string[])` (199), `ConnectToExisting(bool connect = true)` (210).
  - **There is NO method on `IComposeBuilder` that accepts a service definition or model.** It cannot describe services; it only references pre-existing `.yaml` files on disk.
- Impl: `FluentDocker/Builders/InternalBuilders.cs:149` — `internal sealed class ComposeBuilder(FluentDockerKernel kernel, string driverId) : IComposeBuilder, IDriverScopedBuilder`. Backing fields are scalars/lists (`_composeFiles`, `_projectName`, `_environment`, etc., lines 159-176). `ExecuteAsync` (line 234) resolves `IComposeDriver` via `_kernel.SysCtl<Drivers.IComposeDriver>(_driverId)`, builds a `ComposeUpConfig` from those fields (lines 251-269), calls `driver.UpAsync(...)`, and returns a `new Services.Impl.ComposeService(...)` (276). **No YAML is generated; `_composeFiles` are paths passed through verbatim.**

### 1d. Where YAML *content* is handled = NOWHERE (only CLI output is parsed)
- The driver only emits CLI args and parses CLI *output*:
  - Args assembly: `DockerCliComposeDriver.cs:261` — `private static string BuildComposeArgs(ComposeFileConfig config)` → `"compose"` + `foreach (file in config.ComposeFiles) args += $" -f {QuoteArgumentIfNeeded(file)}"` + `-p {ProjectName}` + `--project-directory {ProjectDirectory}` (lines 263-270). This is the **only** place compose files surface, and only as `-f <path>`.
  - Sub-arg builders (all `public static`, in `DockerCliComposeDriver.Args.cs`): `BuildUpSubArgs` (51), `BuildDownSubArgs` (87), `BuildRemoveSubArgs` (21), `BuildListSubArgs` (36, `"ps --format json"`), `BuildRestartSubArgs` (104), `BuildLogsSubArgs` (117), `BuildConfigSubArgs` (138), `BuildBuildSubArgs` (155), `BuildPullSubArgs` (175), `BuildRunSubArgs` (190), `BuildScaleSubArgs` (226), `BuildCreateSubArgs` (239).
  - Output parsing uses **STJ** (`System.Text.Json`) with `JsonHelper.CaseInsensitiveOptions`: `ParseServiceList(string json, ILogger)` at `DockerCliComposeDriver.Args.cs:266` handles a JSON array or NDJSON of `ComposeServiceInfo`; images parsed inline in `DockerCliComposeDriver.Info.cs:136-155`; `top` text-table parsing in `DockerCliComposeDriver.Parsing.cs:21` `ParseTopOutput`. **None of these read compose-file YAML.**
- Config DTOs that flow into the driver live in `FluentDocker/Drivers/ComposeModels.cs`: base `ComposeFileConfig` (line 10) with `List<string> ComposeFiles`, `string ProjectName`, `string ProjectDirectory`, `Dictionary<string,string> Environment`, `List<string> Services`; subtypes `ComposeUpConfig` (27), `ComposeDownConfig` (62), etc. Result/info DTOs (`ComposeServiceInfo` at 337 with `[JsonPropertyName("Service")]` on `Name` line 340, `[JsonPropertyName("ID")]` on `ContainerId` line 349; `ComposeImage` 403; `ComposeProcesses` 390) — these are for parsing CLI JSON, **not** for emitting compose files.

**Bottom line for (1):** services are modeled by `ComposeServiceDefinition` (POCO) but that model is never serialized; the live builder only references on-disk YAML files and shells out to the CLI. To EMIT YAML you must add an emitter — none exists to extend.

## (2) Where a new top-level `models:` element + per-service `models:` binding would slot in

Compose `models:` has two locations (Docker Compose spec): a **top-level `models:` map** (each entry has `model:` ref, optional `context_size`, `runtime_flags`, provider opts) and a **per-service `models:` binding** (list of model names, or a map `model-name: {endpoint_var, model_var}`).

Because no emitter exists, the design splits into model + emitter + wiring:

### 2a. Model classes (mirror existing short/long pattern in `FluentDocker/Model/Compose/`)
- **Per-service binding** (slots into `ComposeServiceDefinition`): add `public IList<IServiceModelDefinition> Models { get; } = [];` alongside the existing get-only collection `Volumes` (`ComposeServiceDefinition.cs:416`). Create marker interface `IServiceModelDefinition` (copy `IServiceVolumeDefinition.cs` verbatim — empty interface), then `ShortServiceModelDefinition { string Entry }` (the `- model-name` list form) and `LongServiceModelDefinition { string Source; string EndpointVar; string ModelVar }` (the map form `model-name: {endpoint_var:, model_var:}`). This is the **identical** pattern to `ShortServiceVolumeDefinition`/`LongServiceVolumeDefinition` and `PortsShort/LongDefinition`.
- **Top-level `models:` map**: a top-level compose document doesn't exist as a class yet (there is NO `ComposeDocument`/`ComposeProjectDefinition` type — verified by grep). If a full-document model is in scope, create `ModelDefinition { string Model; long? ContextSize; IList<string> RuntimeFlags; IDictionary<string,string> ProviderOptions }` and host it in a new top-level document class (e.g. `ComposeProjectDefinition` with `IDictionary<string, ComposeServiceDefinition> Services` and `IDictionary<string, ModelDefinition> Models`). Today services are not aggregated into any document type — `ComposeServiceBuilder._config` is a single, standalone `ComposeServiceDefinition`.

### 2b. The emitter (NEW — there is no existing one to slot into)
- You must author a YAML writer (hand-rolled `StringBuilder`, matching the project's no-extra-deps stance, OR add YamlDotNet — but note the repo currently has zero YAML deps). The emitter walks `ComposeServiceDefinition` → writes `services:` block, and for each service writes a `models:` sub-block; plus a top-level `models:` block. Then it must `File.WriteAllText(tempPath, yaml)` and feed that path into the existing pipeline via `ComposeUpConfig.ComposeFiles` (i.e., the generated file becomes a normal `-f` arg). **This temp-file-then-`-f` bridge is the only way to connect a model to the live CLI driver**, since the driver consumes paths, not content.

### 2c. Builder wiring point
- Per-service fluent: add `Models(params string[])` / `Models(Action<IModelBindingBuilder>)` to `ComposeServiceBuilder` (`ComposeServiceBuilder.cs`), mutating `_config.Models` — same shape as the existing `Volume(...)`/`Ports(...)` methods (lines 37-133).
- Project-level/top-level: this is the gap. `IComposeBuilder` (the wired builder) has no way to accept services or models. Phase 7b must add an entry such as `IComposeBuilder.WithService(string name, Action<ComposeServiceBuilder>)` and `IComposeBuilder.WithModel(string name, Action<IComposeModelSpecBuilder>)`, have `ComposeBuilder.ExecuteAsync` (`InternalBuilders.cs:234`) render the accumulated model graph to a temp YAML file BEFORE building `ComposeUpConfig`, and add the temp path to `_composeFiles`. See §4 for the recommended interface shape.

## (3) The attach-to-existing-project parse path (v3.1, commit 2c3f128 / #341)

**Key finding: the attach feature does NOT parse compose-file YAML at all.** It is identity-by-reference (project name and/or file paths) + CLI-output queries.

- Builder flag: `IComposeBuilder.ConnectToExisting(bool connect = true)` declared at `BuilderInterfaces.cs:210` (XML doc 201-209). Impl: `ComposeBuilder.ConnectToExisting` at `InternalBuilders.cs:232` sets `private bool _attachToExisting` (field at line 175).
- Attach branch in `ComposeBuilder.ExecuteAsync` (`InternalBuilders.cs:241-249`):
  ```csharp
  if (_attachToExisting)
  {
    if (string.IsNullOrEmpty(_projectName) && _composeFiles.Count == 0)
      throw new FluentDockerException(
          "ConnectToExisting requires WithProjectName and/or WithComposeFile to identify the project.");
    return new Services.Impl.ComposeService(
        _kernel, _driverId, _composeFiles, _projectName, _removeVolumes, _removeImages);
  }
  ```
  It **skips `UpAsync`** and constructs a `ComposeService` bound to the (`_composeFiles`, `_projectName`) identity. The compose file is never opened/parsed in C#.
- Target ctor: `FluentDocker/Services/Impl/ComposeService.cs:34-53` — `public ComposeService(FluentDockerKernel kernel, string driverId, List<string> composeFiles, string projectName, bool removeVolumes = false, bool removeImages = false)`. Stores `_composeFiles`/`_projectName`; later ops (`ListServicesAsync` at line 66) build a `ComposeListConfig { ComposeFiles = _composeFiles, ProjectName = _projectName }` and shell out (`docker compose ... ps --format json`), parsing **CLI JSON output** via `ParseServiceList`. State is reconciled by `RefreshStateAsync` (added in #341) off `docker compose ps` status, NOT off the file.
- So "attach" provides **no precedent for reading a compose file's `models:`**. If Phase 7b needs to *read back* `models:` from an existing file, that is a brand-new parse path (there is no compose-file reader anywhere in the repo). The only file-aware step is `WithEnvFile` (`InternalBuilders.cs:190-209`) which line-parses a `.env` file — not YAML.

## (4) How `IComposeModelBuilder` / `IComposeModelSpecBuilder` should hang off the existing `IComposeBuilder`

Follow the established lambda-sub-builder + marker-interface idioms in this codebase.

### Conventions to copy verbatim
- **Lambda sub-builder pattern**: `Builder.UseCompose(Action<IComposeBuilder> configure)` (`Builder.cs:146`) — `new ComposeBuilder(...); configure(builder);`. Mirror this: `IComposeBuilder.WithModel(string name, Action<IComposeModelSpecBuilder> configure)` constructs a spec builder, invokes the lambda, stores result.
- **Fluent return-self interfaces**: every `IComposeBuilder` method returns `IComposeBuilder` (`BuilderInterfaces.cs:97-211`). New methods must too: `IComposeBuilder WithModel(string name, Action<IComposeModelSpecBuilder> configure);` and (per-service) the existing `ComposeServiceBuilder` methods return `ComposeServiceBuilder`.
- **Marker interfaces for polymorphic entries**: empty `IPortsDefinition`/`IServiceVolumeDefinition` (`IPortsDefinition.cs`, `IServiceVolumeDefinition.cs`) with Short/Long impls. Apply to `IServiceModelDefinition` (per-service binding) exactly the same way.
- **Internal sealed builder impl exposing `IDriverScopedBuilder`**: `internal sealed class ComposeBuilder(...) : IComposeBuilder, IDriverScopedBuilder` (`InternalBuilders.cs:149`), exposing `Kernel`/`DriverId` explicitly (lines 155-158) so driver-specific extensions can resolve. Any new sub-builders that need driver awareness should follow this; the model spec builder is pure data and need NOT implement `IDriverScopedBuilder`.

### Recommended shape
- **`IComposeModelSpecBuilder`** = fluent builder for a SINGLE top-level model entry. Methods (all return `IComposeModelSpecBuilder`): `Model(string reference)` (the `model:` OCI/registry ref), `ContextSize(long)`, `RuntimeFlags(params string[])`, and provider option setters. Backed by a `ModelDefinition` POCO in `FluentDocker/Model/Compose/`. This is the analog of `ComposeServiceBuilder` (single `_config`), with `internal` ctor.
- **`IComposeModelBuilder`** (per-service binding) — if you want a richer per-service form than `params string[]`: fluent builder producing `IServiceModelDefinition` entries, e.g. `Bind(string modelName)` → `ShortServiceModelDefinition`, or `Bind(string modelName, string endpointVar, string modelVar)` → `LongServiceModelDefinition`. Hang it off the per-service `ComposeServiceBuilder` via `ComposeServiceBuilder Models(Action<IComposeModelBuilder> configure)` mutating `_config.Models`, mirroring `Volume(...)` (`ComposeServiceBuilder.cs:37`).
- **Top-level wiring onto `IComposeBuilder`**: add `IComposeBuilder WithModel(string name, Action<IComposeModelSpecBuilder> configure)` to `BuilderInterfaces.cs` (after `WithProfiles`/`ConnectToExisting`, ~line 199-210) and implement in `ComposeBuilder` (`InternalBuilders.cs`) by accumulating into a `Dictionary<string, ModelDefinition> _models = []` field (next to `_scale`/`_profiles`, lines 159-176). In `ExecuteAsync` (line 234), BEFORE constructing `ComposeUpConfig`, if any models/services were declared inline, render them to a temp YAML file and `_composeFiles.Add(tempPath)` so the existing `-f` machinery picks them up (`BuildComposeArgs` at `DockerCliComposeDriver.cs:261`). Respect the `_attachToExisting` early-return (lines 241-249) — inline models are incompatible with attach (throw, or skip emission).

### Gotchas / constraints to honor
- **500-line code-file cap** (CLAUDE.md): `ComposeServiceDefinition.cs` is already 419 lines and near-cap-aware; add `Models` property there but keep new model classes in their own files (`ModelDefinition.cs`, `IServiceModelDefinition.cs`, `ShortServiceModelDefinition.cs`, `LongServiceModelDefinition.cs`) like every other entry type. Split the new emitter into a `partial` if it grows.
- **No YAML library present** — adding `models:` emission means either hand-writing YAML or introducing a new package dependency; flag this decision explicitly. Booleans/strings must be quoted per the existing `PortsShortDefinition` doc warning about YAML base-60 parsing.
- The orphaned `ComposeServiceBuilder`/`ComposeServiceDefinition` are the natural home for the model graph, but **wiring them into `Builder.UseCompose`/`IComposeBuilder` is itself net-new work** — there is no `WithService(...)` today. Emitting `models:` "via the existing compose builder" is therefore really "build the missing model→YAML→temp-file→`-f` bridge, then add `models:` to it."
- STJ is the project's JSON tool (`JsonHelper.CaseInsensitiveOptions`, used in `DockerCliComposeDriver.Args.cs:276`); if you parse an existing compose file's `models:` back in, prefer STJ-on-converted-YAML or a YAML lib consistent with whatever you pick for emission. Per MEMORY.md gotcha: `JsonElement.TryGetInt32()` throws on non-Number — guard `ValueKind` first.
